title: Daily Light Integral Calculation
objective: Calculate DLI from constant or time-varying photon flux and identify errors caused by units, sampling, and wavelength-band mismatch.

terms.definition: Daily light integral: accumulated photons per square metre per day, expressed as mol m-2 d-1.
Photon flux density measured at one moment.
Time represented by each logged value in a numerical sum.
Change in photon flux through the light period, especially important under sunlight or dimming.

coreScience: For a constant PPFD, DLI = PPFD x photoperiod hours x 0.0036. The factor converts micromoles per second and hours to moles per day. For example, 500 micromoles m-2 s-1 for 18 hours equals 32.4 mol m-2 d-1. The calculation must retain whether the input is PPFD or ePPFD.

When light changes with clouds, curtains, sunrise, dimming, or control events, DLI must be integrated from logged readings: sum(PFD_i x interval seconds) / 1,000,000. A midday spot reading multiplied by day length can substantially overstate or understate the true integral.

DLI compresses time into a daily total. Equal DLI can come from different intensities and photoperiods, but plants may respond differently because photosynthesis is nonlinear, signaling depends on timing, heat and water loads differ, and dark-period biology is not preserved by the arithmetic.
cultivationRelevance: DLI is useful for comparing delivered photon dose across days and for coordinating greenhouse supplemental lighting with sunlight.
A stage plan should record DLI together with photoperiod, PPFD distribution, spectrum, temperature, carbon dioxide, irrigation, and plant response rather than treating DLI as a standalone recipe.

measureAndRecord.requirement: PAR-DLI or ePAR-DLI, instrument model, and calibration status.
Logging interval, complete timestamps, missing data, daylight-saving handling, and control events.
Sensor position, canopy height, representative area, shading, and whether the sensor moved.
Formula, units, interval weighting, averaging method, and software version.
Stage, cultivar, photoperiod, PPFD map, environment, irrigation, and observed response.

misconceptions: DLI is PPFD with a new label: PPFD is a rate at a moment; DLI is the time-integrated daily dose.
Equal DLI means equal growth: Intensity, duration, spectrum, timing, dark period, and other resources can change the response.
One spot reading gives outdoor DLI: Variable natural light requires time integration with an appropriately placed sensor.
evidenceLimits: Published DLI responses depend on genotype, stage, environment, canopy, and measurement band. A DLI value alone cannot establish a universal cannabis optimum or safety limit.

overview: Daily light integral (DLI) is the time integral of photosynthetic photon flux density at a specified wavelength band. PPFD is an instantaneous rate (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹); DLI is a daily photon dose (mol m⁻² d⁻¹). A daily total does not describe intensity peaks, spectrum or timing.

mechanisms.heading: Constant light
mechanisms.body: DLI = PPFD × hours × 3600 / 1,000,000 = PPFD × hours × 0.0036. For an illustrative constant 500 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ over 18 h, DLI = 32.4 mol m⁻² d⁻¹.

mechanisms.heading: Changing light
mechanisms.body: For samples representing successive intervals, DLI ≈ Σ(PPFDᵢ × Δtᵢ) / 1,000,000, with Δtᵢ in seconds. Averages must be time-weighted when intervals differ; gaps should be flagged rather than silently treated as zero.

mechanisms.heading: Band consistency
mechanisms.body: PAR-based PPFD usually counts 400–700 nm photons; ePPFD uses an extended 400–750 nm range. Keep band and sensor response with every DLI result; unlike units or bands cannot be directly compared.

practicalInterpretation: Use a logged canopy-level sensor or a representative sensor map when light varies over time and space.
Verify timestamp boundaries, sampling interval, missing samples, daylight-saving transitions, and whether the integration covers one complete local day.
Keep photoperiod, light distribution, spectrum and crop conditions alongside DLI; equal daily totals do not imply identical physiological responses.
limitationsAndUncertainty: The illustrative constant-light calculation is arithmetic, not a recommended target for cannabis.
A single sensor may miss spatial gradients, while a spot measurement may miss temporal variation.
Numerical integration approximates a continuous signal; logging frequency, instrument calibration and interpolation assumptions influence accuracy.
